claims.text: Time-dependent plastic-deformation resistance in refractory HEA multilayer coatings is governed by dislocation blocking at chemically sharp, coherent interfaces.
Chemically sharp, coherent interfaces interrupt slip propagation.
Interrupting slip propagation suppresses strain localization.
HfTaTiVZr and TaTiVWZr are refractory high-entropy-alloy systems relevant to time-dependent plastic deformation.
The proposed HfTaTiVZr and TaTiVWZr coatings consist of alternating layers with distinct lattice orientations.
The proposed multilayers possess chemically sharp, coherent interfaces.
Optimized deposition parameters can produce sharp, coherent interfaces, while intentional grading can produce diffuse interfaces.
Nanoindentation creep behavior of HfTaTiVZr and TaTiVWZr can be tested from 298 K to 573 K under static constant-load and dynamic loading.
Time-dependent deformation in HfTaTiVZr and TaTiVWZr is dislocation dominated.
Sharp multilayer interfaces block dislocation nucleation.
Sharp multilayer interfaces block dislocation propagation by interrupting slip-band formation.
Restricting dislocation activity and strain localization reduces time-dependent plastic deformation relative to coatings without clear interfaces.
Sharp-interface multilayers will have lower creep displacement than monolithic HEA coatings and diffuse-interface multilayers.
Sharp-interface multilayers will have higher local yield stress than monolithic HEA coatings and diffuse-interface multilayers.
Only sharp-interface multilayers will significantly impede plastic-strain accumulation in the proposed comparison.
The proposed temperature boundary of 298–573 K is experimentally applicable to HfTaTiVZr and TaTiVWZr creep testing, but its applicability to multilayer-interface effects is not established.
